lines.text: Three weeks before an event, a teammate changes one number. The robot's packed in a crate. Who notices?
A test is a check the computer runs for you, every time the code changes.
Hardware Simulation already ran your program with no robot. A test uses that same simulator, but nothing loops unless the test says so.
This test schedules the command that sends the arm straight up. Scheduling only puts it in line, so the motor still has no request.
Then the test runs the scheduler once. One tick. Now the request names the target, and the check passes.
Leave that tick out, and the check fails. It's the most common mistake in this lesson.
The flywheel test fakes the sensor. It sets the speed just inside the tolerance and checks that it counts, then sets it well outside and checks that it doesn't.
Be the teammate. Widen the tolerance, and run the tests.
The far-off speed slides inside the band, and the second check fails. That edit just got caught.
A test checks the request, not the motion. The bench still has to show the arm really gets there.
Put decisions where a test can read them, and let the computer check them every time.
